1.explanation:
• src/ol/layer/WebGLTile.js – defines the WebGLTile layer’s tile management and styling. It doesn’t hook into the reprojection pipeline (ol/reproj) when the source projection differs from the view.

• src/ol/render/webgl/TileLayer.js – implements the WebGL renderer for Tile layers. It generates quads in view coordinates but never invokes the reproj/Tile code to triangulate or warp a source tile in a differing CRS.

• src/ol/reproj/Tile.js – contains the logic for reprojecting raster tiles (triangulation, vertex buffers, etc.). It’s used by the Canvas renderer but is not wired into the WebGLTile and its WebGL renderer.

• src/ol/source/GeoTIFF.js – reads the COG’s native projection metadata and exposes a projection option. The WebGLTile layer currently ignores this projection field, so it cannot trigger reprojection when rendering.

By updating WebGLTile.js and its WebGL renderer (render/webgl/TileLayer.js) to use the reproj/Tile pipeline (in reproj/Tile.js) and honoring the source.projection set by GeoTIFF.js, WebGLTile layers will automatically reproject COGs in arbitrary CRSs onto the map’s view projection.
1.bug_scenario: The reporter is trying to display a Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFF (COG) stored in a UTM zone (EPSG:32636) on a map whose view projection is EPSG:4326 (or EPSG:3857) by using ol.source.GeoTIFF with an ol.layer.WebGLTile. When they omit the manual “projection” option on the GeoTIFF source, the COG never appears on the map. OSM tiles load fine and the view can be fitted to the COG’s native extent, but the WebGLTile layer does not perform automatic reprojection the way the built-in Image/GDI layers do. As a result, no tiles render for the EPSG:32636 source in the WebGLTile layer.

2.explanation:
• src/ol/source/GeoTIFF.js defines the GeoTIFF tile source and reads the source projection but never applies reprojection for WebGL-based layers.  
• src/ol/layer/WebGLTile.js implements the WebGLTile layer and ignores any projection parameter on its source, so it never requests reprojected tiles.  
• src/ol/renderer/webgl/TileLayer.js is responsible for feeding tiles to the WebGL shader pipeline; it only handles tiles already in the view projection and has no reprojection step.  
• src/ol/reproj/Tile.js contains the logic for canvas-based reprojection of tiles but is not invoked anywhere in the WebGL tile rendering path.  
• src/ol/source/Tile.js orchestrates reprojection when a source projection differs from the view but only in the canvas renderer, so WebGLTile consumers never get reprojected data.
2.bug_scenario: The user is trying to display a Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF (COG) in EPSG:32636 (UTM zone 36) on a map whose view projection is EPSG:4326 (or WebMercator 3857), using a WebGLTile layer. While the OSM base layer renders correctly and fitting the view to the COG extent works, the COG itself never appears. In the HTML repro the user even registers the UTM projection via proj4 and tries passing it via a commented-out “projection” option to the GeoTIFF source. The root cause is that reprojection of GeoTIFF tiles is supported in the canvas pipeline but is not wired into the WebGLTile layer, so no pixels ever get drawn when the source projection differs from the view projection.
